t: Subrogation and contribution are described as corollaries of which principle of insurance?
e: Indemnity is the essence of the fire contract; subrogation and contribution exist to ensure the insured does not recover more than the loss.

t: A paint factory's annual SFSP premium is ₹90. The premium actually chargeable is
e: AIFT Rule 6: minimum premium is ₹100 per policy, except ₹50 for risks rateable under Section III and tiny sector industries under Section IV.

t: A policy is cancelled mid-term because the building insured was demolished by the insured. Refund of premium should be
o: Allowed on pro-rata basis for the unexpired period
Allowed at 50% of the unexpired premium
e: N.B. to AIFT Rule 10: where a policy is cancelled due to a Government order, completion of a building in course of construction or demolition of buildings, pro-rata refund may be allowed.

t: Which of the following is excluded under the Subsidence and Landslide peril of SFSP?
o: Settlement or movement of made-up ground
Subsidence of part of the site on which the property stands
Rock slide damaging the factory roof
e: Exclusions: normal cracking, settlement or bedding down of new structures; settlement of made-up ground; coastal or river erosion; defective design/workmanship/materials; demolition, construction or excavation works.

t: A fire claim under SFSP is assessed at ₹40 lakh. The insured has incurred architects' fees of ₹2 lakh and debris removal cost of ₹1 lakh. Without any add-on, the amount payable towards these two items is
e: Architects, surveyors and consulting engineers' fees are covered up to 3% of the claim (₹1,20,000) and debris removal up to 1% (₹40,000); total ₹1,60,000. Higher amounts need the add-on covers.

t: Machinery temporarily removed from the insured premises for repairs is covered under SFSP for a period not exceeding
e: Property removed to any other building is excluded, except machinery and equipment temporarily removed for repairs, cleaning, renovation or similar purposes for not more than 60 days.

t: Under Condition 5 of the SFSP policy, the insurer may cancel the policy by giving notice of
o: 15 days, refunding pro-rata premium for the unexpired term
e: Condition 5: the insured may cancel at any time (short-period retention); the insurer may cancel on 15 days' notice with rateable (pro-rata) refund for the unexpired term.

t: Long-term fire policies for a period exceeding 12 months may be issued only for
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). AIFT General Rule 3: policies exceeding 12 months shall not be issued except for dwellings; refund is not allowed for reduction of SI under such long-term policies.

t: Property worth ₹10 lakh is insured with three insurers for ₹2 lakh, ₹5 lakh and ₹3 lakh. A loss of ₹1 lakh occurs. The first insurer (₹2 lakh) pays
e: Condition 11 (contribution): each insurer pays its rateable proportion, here in the ratio 2:5:3, so the first insurer pays 1,00,000 × 2/10 = ₹20,000.

t: Under Condition 13 (Arbitration) of the SFSP policy, a dispute can be referred to arbitration only when
o: Both parties agree to waive court proceedings
The insurer has repudiated the claim
Liability is admitted and the dispute relates only to quantum
e: Arbitration under Condition 13 is available for differences as to quantum where liability is otherwise admitted; if the insurer disputes liability, the matter is not referable to arbitration.

t: Which of the following CANNOT be insured on reinstatement value basis?
e: Reinstatement value insurance may be granted on buildings, machinery and furniture, fixtures and fittings only; stocks are always insured on market value basis.

t: Under the Deterioration of Stocks in Cold Storage add-on (power failure at the power station), the insurer is not liable unless each failure of supply exceeds
e: Both versions of the cold storage deterioration add-on require that the duration of each failure of electric supply exceeds 24 hours; the power-station version is rated at 25% of the policy rate on the stock SI.

t: The additional premium for the Escalation Clause is charged at
o: 50% of the full rate on the selected percentage increase
25% of the full rate on the policy sum insured
A flat ₹0.10‰ on the escalated sum insured
100% of the full rate on the selected percentage increase
e: AIFT Rule 12(b): additional premium payable in advance at 50% of the full rate on the selected percentage increase, which cannot exceed 25% of the SI.

t: A declaration policy for stock was issued with SI ₹1 crore and provisional premium ₹2,000. Declarations averaged ₹40 lakh over the year. The refund admissible is
e: Premium on average SI = 2,000 × 40/100 = ₹800, so the difference is ₹1,200; but refund is restricted to 50% of the provisional premium, i.e. ₹1,000.

t: If the insured fails to submit a monthly declaration by the last day of the succeeding month, the value at risk for that month is deemed to be
o: The full sum insured under the policy
The average of the previous declarations
e: AIFT Rule 14(b)/Declaration Clause: if a declaration is not received within the specified period, the full SI under the policy is deemed to have been declared.

t: A bakery's monthly sales are ₹60,000, cost of flour ₹12,000 and fixed monthly expenses ₹8,000. The gross profit for a Fire LOP policy is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). GP by difference basis = Turnover − variable expenses = 60,000 − 12,000 = ₹48,000; equivalently net profit 40,000 + standing charges 8,000 = ₹48,000 (addition basis).

t: The minimum retention of premium under a Floater Declaration policy is
e: AIFT Rule 15: floater declaration policies need minimum SI ₹2 crore and minimum retention of 80% of the annual premium, i.e. maximum refund 20%.

t: The Contract Price Insurance Clause can be attached only to a policy covering
o: Stocks in process at the insured's factory
Imported goods sold but not delivered, where the sale contract is cancelled by reason of the insured perils
Goods of local manufacture held in a bonded warehouse
Goods held in trust by a transporter
e: The clause applies only to imported goods (not local manufacture); liability is based on contract price when the sale contract is cancelled wholly or partly due to loss by an insured peril.

t: With effect from 1 April 2021, which risks continue to be governed by the erstwhile AIFT 2001?
o: Risks (other than dwellings) where the total value at risk exceeds ₹50 crore at any one location
All risks with sum insured up to ₹5 crore
All dwellings irrespective of sum insured
e: IRDAI notification of 28 December 2020 de-notified the AIFT for dwellings (any SI) and other risks up to ₹50 crore per location from 1 April 2021; larger risks continue under AIFT until further notification.

t: Under Bharat Sookshma Udyam Suraksha, the excess applicable to each claim (other than terrorism) is
o: 5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹25,000
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹10,000
e: BSUS carries a flat excess of ₹5,000; Bharat Laghu Udyam Suraksha carries 5% of each claim subject to a minimum of ₹10,000 (other than terrorism).

t: Which type of fire extinguishing appliance is appropriate for fires involving flammable liquids of the oil and gasoline type?
e: Foam is used for oil/gasoline type flammable liquid fires; CO2 and dry chemical extinguishers are suited to electrical equipment and flammable liquids.

t: Under the RDSAFER sequence in a fire claim, which item is stated to be not applicable to fire policies?
e: RDSAFER: Reinstatement value, Depreciation, Salvage, Average, Franchise (not applicable to fire policies), Excess, Reinstatement premium.

t: An IAR policy insured's loss is ₹50 lakh and under-insurance is found to be 12%. The under-insurance deduction is
o: Nil, as under-insurance up to 15% is waived
e: IAR special condition: under-insurance up to 15% is waived; if it exceeds 15%, the full under-insurance is applied.

t: Standard turnover ₹20 crore, trend in turnover +10%, rate of gross profit 30%, turnover achieved during the indemnity period ₹10 crore. The loss of gross profit is
e: Adjusted standard turnover = 20 × 1.10 = ₹22 crore; reduction = 22 − 10 = ₹12 crore; loss of GP = 12 × 30% = ₹3.6 crore.

t: Testing and commissioning risks are an inbuilt cover under
e: EAR provides erection and testing coverage; CAR covers civil works and has no testing cover.

t: An EAR policy's period of insurance commences from
o: The date of completion of civil works
The date of payment of premium
The date of shipment of the first consignment
The date of arrival of the first consignment at site or the start of any project-related work at site, whichever is earlier
e: Cover runs from arrival of the first consignment at site / start of project work and ends on the date of expiry or commercial production (EAR) or handing over to the principal (CAR).

t: An annual SFSP policy (premium ₹12,000) is cancelled at the insured's request after exactly 4 months. The refund due is
e: ★ Key fact (repeated across the mocks of this paper). Cancellation at the insured's option: premium retained at the short-period scale – 50% for 4 months = ₹6,000 retained, so ₹6,000 refunded.

t: Pre-operative expenses such as construction of temporary roads and sheds form part of the sum insured under
e: Recurring pre-operative expenses can be part of CAR SI; non-recurring items like consultancy and licence fees need not be part of EAR SI.

t: On completion of a project, the EAR premium can be adjusted on the basis of actual values of
o: Prime cost of plant and machinery
Freight, customs duty, handling charges and cost of erection
e: Premium adjustment after expiry is possible for freight, customs duty, handling charges and erection cost; not for prime cost of P&M or escalation premium.

t: A 30-month CAR policy project is completed 5 months early with a claims ratio of 40%. Refund of premium for early completion is
o: Admissible only if there are no claims at all
Admissible only if completion is at least 6 months early
Not admissible, as refunds are never allowed under project policies
Admissible, since the period exceeds 18 months, claims are below 60% and the unexpired period is at least 3 months
e: Refund for early completion requires policy period more than 18 months, claims experience below 60% and a minimum unexpired period of 3 months.

t: Which of the following is an exclusion specific to the CAR policy and not listed under EAR exclusions?
o: Loss discovered at the time of inventory
e: CAR additionally excludes files/drawings/cheques, packing material, vehicles licensed for road use, penalties under contract and breakage of glass (the last being available as an add-on).

t: For an EAR policy with SI ₹80 crore at an unprotected site, the excess for a fire claim during the storage/erection period is
o: 20% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of the testing period excess, with an upper limit of ₹3 crore
10% of the claim amount subject to a minimum of the testing period excess, with an upper limit of ₹2 crore
10% of the claim amount with an upper limit of ₹5 crore
e: Fire at unprotected sites: SI below ₹50 crore – 10% of claim (min testing excess, cap ₹2 crore); SI above ₹50 crore – 20% of claim (min testing excess, cap ₹3 crore).

t: Which maintenance cover under EAR/CAR covers damage occurring during the maintenance period provided it was caused during the erection period?
e: Maintenance visits cover is limited to damage caused by the contractor while carrying out maintenance obligations; extended maintenance additionally covers damage during the maintenance period caused during erection. Both can be granted only at inception.

t: An EAR policy can be cancelled at the insured's request only if, among other conditions,
o: The principal gives a no-objection certificate
The claims experience is below 75% of premium
The testing period has not commenced
At least 50% of the policy period is unexpired
e: Conditions: claims experience below 60% of reworked premium; unexpired period not less than 3 months or 25% of the policy period, whichever is less; and testing should not have commenced.

t: For faulty design, the basic CAR policy provides cover equivalent to
o: DE1 – outright exclusion of all design-related loss or damage
e: The basic CAR excludes faulty design entirely (DE1), while for defective material and workmanship it gives the equivalent of DE4; DE2, DE3 and DE4 are available as add-ons for design.

t: The permitted limit of foreign direct investment in an Indian insurance company is currently:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). Raised from 49% to 74% by the Insurance (Amendment) Act 2021; intermediaries may have 100%.

t: Under EAR/CAR, in the case of a total loss the basis of settlement is
o: The replacement value of the item as new
The actual value of the item immediately before the loss, less salvage
The contract value of the item plus escalation
The sum insured for the item
e: Repairable damage: cost of repairs to restore to the pre-loss condition less salvage; total loss: actual value immediately before the loss less salvage, to the extent included in the SI.

t: The sum insured under an Advance Loss of Profit policy represents
o: The loan amount sanctioned by the financier
Anticipated turnover for the first year
Anticipated gross profit for the indemnity period selected
e: ALOP covers the financial consequences of delay in commercial operations due to insured damage under CAR/EAR; SI is the anticipated GP for the IP, based on the project's financial model, and only one claim is payable.

t: Which of the following is a cause of loss covered under an MBD policy?
o: Entry of foreign material into the machine
Defects known to the insured at inception
Gradually developing cracks not necessitating immediate stoppage
e: MBD covers unforeseen accidental breakdown from short circuit, entry of foreign bodies, negligence, lubrication failure, insulation and metallurgical failure; gradually developing defects, known defects and boiler explosions are excluded.

t: When insuring a turbo-generator under MBD, which break-up of values is acceptable?
o: Turbine, alternator, gear box, control panel and cables
e: Parts of machines should not be insured separately; for TG sets only the break-up into turbine, alternator, gear box, control panel and cables is acceptable. Gear boxes must be insured with the drive or driven equipment.

t: In an MBD partial loss claim, depreciation is deducted
o: On the entire machine according to its age
Only on parts with limited life specified by the manufacturer or subject to wear and tear
On all replaced parts at 10% per year
e: Partial loss: cost of restoring the machine to its former state with no depreciation, except for limited-life/wear-and-tear parts; total loss: actual value immediately before the loss.

t: The reinstatement premium after an MBD claim is calculated on pro-rata basis from
o: The date of claim settlement for a full year
The date of loss until expiry of the policy
The date of inception until expiry of the policy
The date the repaired item is again put to work until expiry of the policy
e: Under MBD the reinstatement premium runs from the date the repaired item is put back to work till expiry, unlike fire where it runs from the date of loss.

t: Which of the following is excluded under Section I of an EEI policy?
o: Scratches on painted or polished surfaces
e: EEI Section I covers fire, lightning, EQ, short circuit, over-voltage, flood, breakdown, burglary, theft and impact; it excludes wear and tear, pre-existing defects, failure of gas/water supply, aesthetic defects, bulbs/valves and consequential loss.

t: A recovery boiler in a paper mill explodes due to smelt–water reaction. Under the BPP policy this is
o: Excluded as a flue gas explosion
Covered only under the MBD policy
Covered, as smelt–water explosion in recovery boilers is specifically covered
e: Chemical explosion is excluded under BPP, but in recovery boilers explosion due to smelt–water reaction is covered.

t: Machinery insured under CPM for an individual value of ₹8 lakh is damaged by flood. The claim is ₹1,00,000. The excess applicable is
e: CPM AOG excess for individual value over ₹5 lakh up to ₹10 lakh: 3% of SI subject to a minimum of ₹25,000; 3% of ₹8 lakh = ₹24,000, so the minimum ₹25,000 applies.

t: Which policy must be in force on the refrigeration machinery before a Deterioration of Stocks policy is issued to a cold storage?
e: DOS is issued only where the cold storage machinery is insured under MBD, since the cover responds to rise in temperature following breakdown of the refrigeration plant.

t: Under the IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests) Regulations 2024, the free-look period for a policy with a term of one year or more is:
e: ★ Core fact (asked across III papers). 30 days from receipt of the policy document, irrespective of the sales channel.

t: A declaration basis DOS policy may be issued only if
o: The policy period is at least 7 months and monthly declarations are made
The policy period is 12 months and the value of stock exceeds ₹50 lakh, with fortnightly declarations
The cold storage has stand-by DG sets
e: DOS declaration policies need a 12-month period, stock value above ₹50 lakh and fortnightly declarations; refund is limited to 50%. The minimum DOS policy period otherwise is 7 months.

t: The minimum deductible for an MBD policy per the circular is
o: 1% of the sum insured of each machine subject to a minimum of ₹2,500
5% of the claim subject to a minimum of ₹10,000
2% of the sum insured subject to a minimum of ₹1,500
e: MBD: 1% of SI of each machine, minimum ₹2,500; the SI must be declared for the machine as a whole and not apportioned to parts.

t: The ALOP time excess for a specialised risk such as a hydro-power or tunnel project is
o: 30 days for the first year plus 1 day per erection month beyond 12, not exceeding 60 days
45 days for the first year plus 1 day for each erection month beyond 12 months, not exceeding 75 days
e: ALOP time excess: ordinary projects 30 days + 1 day per erection month beyond 12 (max 60 days); specialised risks and combined-cycle/gas power plants 45 days + 1 day (max 75 days).
